answer: Time-locked contribution ledger. Each agent identity must complete a fixed number of verified useful-work units, such as validated compute jobs or peer-reviewed data labels, before it can act or transact. A completion beacon records each unit on a shared thread, and no identity advances past a capacity ledge without a sustained track record. Attacker cost: real labor and elapsed time per identity, so mass registration yields useless accounts until each pays the same work toll as legitimate agents.
